claim: html-to-text.spec.ts 'stays linear on many <style prefixes' (js/polynomial-redos) keeps the shape that replaced the one Date.now() reading per size that failed CI run 37268845925 (65 vs <64) on a PR that never touched html-to-text. The command checks exactly this. First it removes, from the whole file and as plain text, every /* ... */ span and everything from // to the end of a line; it then reads only what is left, so a test wrapped in /* */ or // comments counts as absent. In what is left: no it, test or describe followed (spaces allowed) by a dot and skip, only, todo or failing, and no xit(, xtest(, xdescribe(, fit(, fdescribe( or ftest( after a non-identifier character ($ and . count as non-identifier). Then the first remaining it("stays linear on many is the test, its body running to the next line that is exactly four spaces and });. That body must hold each of these as a whole line - const inputs = [250, 4000].map((n) => "<style".repeat(n)); const best = [Infinity, Infinity]; the for (let round = 0; round < 20; round++) loop head; const start = performance.now(); htmlToText(input); the best[k] = Math.min(best[k], performance.now() - start) update; const [small, large] = best; expect(large).toBeLessThan(small * 64); - plus exactly one expect(, exactly 4 occurrences of best, and none of the words return, if, while, try or Date. It is a tripwire against reverting or switching off that shape, not a proof the test works. Because the removal is textual, a // or /* inside a string literal hides the code after it (so an early return can slip through, and jest has no hasAssertions to catch it). It also misses chained forms such as test.concurrent.only and any edit that keeps those lines live but defeats them (an expect in a function never called, both sizes timing one input, a shadowed htmlToText, Math or performance, a jest.mock of the module). It trips falsely on a .fit( method call or fit( inside a string, on prose such as test. only outside a comment, and when a // comment contains /* (the /* */ removal runs first and can swallow code up to the next */). That the old /<style[^>]*>[\s\S]*?<\/style>/gi replace fails the test (ratio 239x or more against the 64x bound) is a recorded mutation result (author on Node 22; audit of PR #629, round 1, on Node 20.20.0), not re-run here. ADR 0100 review trail, 2026-10-05.
